title: CLO X KASHION Kaixin CLO User Story
description: CLO X KASHION Kaixin CLO User Story
transcript:
How to use the print on the pattern?  
It is very difficult for the client to understand the final effect of the print on the pattern.  
Previously, we used to sell the print in silver or create the existing pattern online,  
and then apply the effect to show it to the client.  
In this case, it was both time-consuming and labor-intensive, and not intuitive.  
It was difficult to determine the final size.  
Now, we can show it to the client directly and efficiently.  
Like this, this is the final effect of the print on the pattern we want to show to the client.  
This way, it is more intuitive and the final size can be known directly.  

I am a designer from Kaixin.  
My daily work is to design and develop according to the client's needs.  
As a designer,  
the most painful part of my previous work was communicating with the client.  
The client's understanding of the pattern was often biased,  
and it was difficult to translate the designer’s vision in communication.  
Often, we had to wait for the sample to be made and then communicate and modify it face-to-face.  

Now that we have 3D, the whole process becomes very simple.  
With 70% of the design completed, we can directly confirm it through 3D,  
make a precise sample, and quickly recommend it to the client.  
We can even create a quick version for some clients.  
Or we can use 3D to produce a 3D design  
that can be directly confirmed by both the client and the designer in 3D.  

I believe that in the future, 3D will help us work more simply and easily.  

I am a designer from Kaixin.  
I am mainly responsible for 3D production in France.  
I used to need a week to make a sample,  
but now I can produce a 3D model in one or two hours.  
I can send it directly to them for confirmation.  
It is more convenient to modify,  
and there is no need to waste so much manpower and physical effort.  
Now that there are more 3D designs,  
I can modify some of the designs myself.  
I find the high-effectiveness of different materials interesting.  
I have a better understanding of some of the techniques.  

I am mainly responsible for the work of a French office designer.  
Due to differences in language, professional knowledge,  
geography and culture, and different ways of thinking,  
communication has always been a big problem.  
After using the 3D system,  
confirmation has become very intuitive.  
Technical problems are very easy to communicate.  

Moreover, I am very happy that the initial phase of the 3D design  
has been converted into a 3D template.  
The designer is very happy.  
At the same time, the cost of developing the related fabric and sewing is significantly reduced.  
The cycle for developing a style has also been shortened to several days.

chunks.content: ## Visualizing Print on Pattern: Enhancing Client Communication This section explains how Kaixin uses 3D technology to present prints on patterns more effectively, improving client understanding and reducing ambiguity around final product appearance and size. Traditionally, it was challenging for clients to grasp the final effect of a print on a pattern. Previously, the process involved selling the print design in silver or creating an existing pattern online, then applying the print effect digitally to show clients. This method was time-consuming, labor-intensive, and lacked intuitiveness. It was also difficult to accurately determine the final size of the print on the pattern. With the new approach, designers can now directly and efficiently show clients the final effect of the print on the pattern in a more intuitive way. This visualization enables clients to see the precise size and appearance without ambiguity, facilitating clearer communication and faster decision-making. --- ## Designer Perspective: Streamlining Communication and Sample Development with 3D This section covers how 3D design technology addresses communication challenges between designers and clients, improving workflow efficiency and reducing the need for physical samples. A designer from Kaixin describes their daily work of designing and developing products based on client needs. A major challenge previously was the communication gap, as clients often had a biased or incomplete understanding of the pattern, making it difficult to convey the designer’s vision. Typically, they had to wait for physical samples to be created before discussing and modifying designs face-to-face, which delayed the process. The introduction of 3D technology simplifies this process. With about 70% of the design completed, designers can use 3D models to confirm details directly with clients, enabling precise sample creation and faster recommendations. They can also produce quick versions or fully detailed 3D designs that clients and designers can jointly review and confirm virtually. The designer expresses optimism that 3D technology will continue to simplify and streamline their work in the future. --- ## Efficiency Gains in 3D Sample Production and Material Effects This section details how 3D modeling reduces sample production time, facilitates easy modifications, and enhances understanding of material effects. A Kaixin designer responsible for 3D production in France explains that while it used to take a week to make a physical sample, they can now produce a 3D model within one or two hours. These models can be sent directly to clients for confirmation, making the modification process more convenient and less resource-intensive. With the increasing volume of 3D designs, the designer can independently modify designs and explore the high-effectiveness of different materials using the 3D models. This hands-on experience has improved their understanding of various technical techniques involved in design. --- ## Overcoming Communication Barriers and Reducing Development Costs with 3D This section highlights how 3D systems help overcome cross-cultural and language barriers, improve technical communication, and reduce costs and development cycles. A designer working in Kaixin’s French office describes how language differences, professional knowledge gaps, geography, culture, and differing thought processes have historically created significant communication challenges.

chunks.content: With the increasing volume of 3D designs, the designer can independently modify designs and explore the high-effectiveness of different materials using the 3D models. This hands-on experience has improved their understanding of various technical techniques involved in design. --- ## Overcoming Communication Barriers and Reducing Development Costs with 3D This section highlights how 3D systems help overcome cross-cultural and language barriers, improve technical communication, and reduce costs and development cycles. A designer working in Kaixin’s French office describes how language differences, professional knowledge gaps, geography, culture, and differing thought processes have historically created significant communication challenges. Since adopting the 3D system, confirmations have become much more intuitive, and technical issues are easier to discuss. The initial phase of 3D design has been converted into reusable 3D templates, which has been well received by designers. This shift has significantly reduced the costs associated with fabric and sewing development and shortened the style development cycle from weeks to just several days, improving overall efficiency and collaboration.
